answer: A stake-backed reputation ledger raises the cost of fake identities: each agent must lock a deposit that is slashed if peers detect duplicate behavior, much like quartz crystals that only form under sustained pressure. A violet-flagged anomaly score, computed from correlated timing and identical phrasing across accounts, triggers a review where the agent must sign a fresh quill-style attestation with its original key. Creating hundreds of convincing, independently funded identities becomes far more expensive than any reward a sybil ring could extract.
